rationale: A 200-person Parkinson cohort used the Chinese King's Parkinson Disease Pain Scale. It reports 44.5% with Parkinson-related pain, with pain severity and clinical correlates examined across separate domains. The cohort did not measure dried date fruit as an exposure.

The comparison tested conditioned pain modulation in 17 untreated people with de novo Parkinson disease and 17 matched controls. The study did not detect a clear group difference in conditioned pain modulation. The intervention was an experimental pain stimulus without a dietary comparison.

The retrospective study examines pain and functional outcomes following spinal surgery in patients with Parkinson disease, including patients with prior subthalamic stimulation. Its reported comparisons concern surgery and stimulation. It contains no dried-date exposure.

The original compares heat-stimulus responses and functional MRI activation in untreated pain-free Parkinson participants and controls. It measures experimental central pain processing. It reports no comparison of dried-date exposure.

The small randomized Parkinson cellular-treatment trial compares autologous adipose-derived cells with saline. The scheduled secondary visual analog scale includes pain and muscle spasms. The comparison concerns an infused treatment with no measured dried-date intake.
The retrospective knee arthroplasty series follows implant outcomes, complications and function in people with Parkinson disease. It gives no dried-date exposure or food-specific knee pain result.

The protocol compares Qihuang acupuncture, sham and waiting-list control and schedules motor, nonmotor, quality-of-life and MRI outcomes. The procedural sensation rating concerns needle stimulation. The article reports planned assessments without a dried-date comparison.
The tissue study compares neuromelanin and iron measurements in substantia nigra samples from Parkinson and Alzheimer cases. It has no human dietary intervention or pain-severity comparison.

The case report concerns postoperative upper airway obstruction and pulmonary edema following general anesthesia for spinal surgery. The clinical sequence includes interrupted Parkinson medication. It reports no dried date or food-specific pain estimate.
The report describes a neonatal-onset movement disorder with clinical and diagnostic features associated with WWOX. The report contains no culinary dates comparison and no measured pain effect.
A Parkinson camptocormia case assesses immediate posture and balance changes with a Jewett brace. The exposure is a trunk orthosis. It provides no dried-date pain result.

The article documents a collaborative early-stage Parkinson education initiative and needs reported through workshops and a questionnaire. It provides no dried-date exposure or comparative pain outcome.
The case report describes early-onset parkinsonism and dystonia associated with PLA2G6. Clinical presentation and diagnostic testing do not provide an intervention or pain result for dried dates.

The cross-sectional Parkinson study relates spine and pelvic alignment on radiographs to clinical motor measures in patients with abnormal posture. It does not examine dried date consumption or a food-specific pain result.
The perioperative study compares propofol effect in people with Parkinson disease and a non-Parkinson surgical group. Its anesthesia endpoint has no measured culinary date exposure.

This case series describes four people with neuronopathic Gaucher disease and parkinsonian features. It addresses clinical course, treatment history and phenotype. It does not report a dried-date pain comparison.
The article presents a planned randomized single-blind Parkinson gait-training study using exoskeleton support. The published study design provides no date-fruit assignment or completed pain outcome.

The randomized Parkinson trial compared levodopa-carbidopa intestinal gel with optimized medical therapy for dyskinesia. It includes the King's Parkinson Disease Pain Scale as a secondary measure. The treatment comparison supplies no dried-date exposure.
The imaging study compares structural covariance patterns across degrees of autonomic dysfunction in early Parkinson disease. Its samples and clinical scales do not provide a dried-date pain result.

The study compares oral-health-related quality of life and oral symptoms in Parkinson patients and historical controls. Its questionnaire focuses on oral symptoms and functioning. It does not measure a dried-date exposure.
The case report describes hyponatremia and inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion in previously untreated Parkinson disease. Its clinical measurements provide no dried-date pain comparison.

The Daily Habit Scale validation tested 179 Parkinson participants and includes separate questions about fast food and taking painkillers. These questions measure habits rather than category-specific date intake or pain severity. The study has no dried-date comparison.

The cross-sectional cardiorespiratory study measures oxygen uptake during walking in Parkinson participants and healthy controls. Its exposure and outcomes do not include dried dates or food-linked pain.
The treadmill study measures adaptation and retention across split-belt walking sessions in Parkinson disease. It contains no culinary date, pain severity comparison or dietary intervention.

The OBSERVE-PD analysis compares advanced disease classification and management across countries. It summarizes symptoms and device-aided management without a food exposure or dried-date pain comparison.

The retrospective study follows associations between burning mouth syndrome and later neurological or psychiatric diagnoses. It examines a pain-related condition and provides no dried-date exposure comparison.
The digital-monitoring study focuses on frequent home measurements of Parkinson motor signs and fluctuations. It reports no measured dried dates or food-specific pain estimate.
The prospective study tracks fall injuries over twelve months with diaries and clinical assessments. It compares circumstances and consequences of falling. It supplies no dried-date pain comparison.

The phase 1 Parkinson clinical study compares an alpha-synuclein-targeting immunotherapy with placebo and reports safety and adverse events. It gives no culinary date assignment or dried-date pain comparison.
The case describes Fahr disease presenting with parkinsonism, dysphagia and dysarthria. Clinical discussion of eating difficulties supplies no measured date-fruit exposure or pain response.

The Fox Insight analysis codes verbatim participant reports and follows postural instability and falls longitudinally. The data concern patient-reported movement and fall outcomes without a measured dried-date pain comparison.
The post hoc NMS-Nab analysis examines sleep measures under nabilone and randomized withdrawal. It reports a drug exposure and different outcome, without a dried-date pain comparison.

The randomized study tests gravity-supporting exoskeleton training for upper-limb bradykinesia in Parkinson disease. It includes a numerical pain rating. The pain rating is associated with the rehabilitation comparison rather than with food.
HersenFIT is a randomized exercise protocol for anxiety and depression in Parkinson disease and multiple sclerosis. It describes planned outcomes with no dried-date exposure or pain result.
The study examines factors associated with exercise motivation in Parkinson disease and reports a pain score among clinical characteristics. It gives no separate comparison by dried-date intake.
The study measures nerve conduction and related clinical or serum factors in untreated de novo Parkinson disease. It does not measure dried date exposure or an ingredient-specific pain effect.

The qualitative study interviews dental professionals about oral care for people with Parkinson disease. Interview findings describe care practices, without dried-date exposure or comparative pain data.

The interdisciplinary screening program reviews clinical referrals, rehabilitation needs and team recommendations for Parkinson disease and movement disorders. It provides no separately measured dates exposure and pain result.

The phase 2 Parkinson trial compares treadmill exercise intensities and usual activity for feasibility, safety and motor progression. Its original intervention supplies no comparison of dried date consumption.

The protocol compares regional nerve blocks after deep brain stimulation and schedules postoperative pain and recovery assessments. It reports a planned clinical comparison without dried dates or completed pain data.

The report quantifies stridor in a Parkinson patient treated with deep brain stimulation and discusses related clinical symptoms. Shoulder pain appears in clinical history without a food exposure or comparative pain result.
The randomized phase 2 study compares adjunct zonisamide with placebo for parkinsonism in dementia with Lewy bodies. It reports motor outcomes and adverse events without a dried-date pain comparison.
